articles.title_orig: Two Nordic leaders urge Putin to end Ukraine war in rare direct contact by Europeans
articles.title_zh: Two Nordic leaders urge Putin to end Ukraine war in rare direct contact by Europeans
articles.content_orig:

President Vladimir Putin received a joint call from the leaders of Norway and Finland on Tuesday as they urged him to end the war in Ukraine, sparking rare contact between Europe and Russia.
The aim of the call, initiated by the offices of President Alexander Stubb and Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store, was to look at “future negotiations to help end the war”.
Store said he and Stubb “stressed the importance of de-escalation” as both leaders voiced strong support for Ukraine, speaking to President Volodymyr Zelensky straight after Putin.
Tuesday’s “frank and substantive” 90 minute phone call was conducted from Helsinki, Finland’s capital, and showed “big differences in views”, according to Store
Following the call, Putin said the duration of the conflict , which has been raging on for four years, has been prolonged by “confrontational” EU and NATO policies, and that a “just and lasting peace” would only be possible if Russia’s interests were considered.
Moscow and Kyiv remain far apart on how to end the war that began with Russia's invasion in February 2022, and long-range airstrikes by both sides have increased this year while battle lines have remained largely static.
"The discussion (with Putin) was frank and substantive. We are neighbouring countries to Russia. The outcome of this war will have a direct impact ⁠on our and the broader European security. Ending the war requires direct discussions," Stubb said.
The Kremlin's readout of the call did not suggest any softening of Putin's position.
"It was emphasised that achieving a just and long-term peace is possible only if the legitimate interests of the Russian Federation are fully and unconditionally taken into account," it said.
"At the same time, ⁠attention was drawn to the confrontational policies of EU and NATO countries, which are contributing to the prolongation of the hostilities."
Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said Tuesday's call had offered nothing new on the `Ukraine conflict, which he said was likely to escalate, and that European countries were simply seeking a role in the negotiation process.
Western European leaders have mostly refused to talk to Putin, hoping to isolate him. But they have been sidelined in peace efforts led by US President Donald Trump, who is seen in many European capitals as unpredictable and prone to side with Putin at Ukraine's expense.
That perception has been reinforced by deals this month in which Putin agreed to supply Russian diesel to the United States and Trump eased sanctions on Russia.
Ukraine has also complained of disruption to intelligence-sharing by the US and to satellite internet services on which its military relies.
Gerhard Mangott, an Austrian political analyst, said European governments had "manoeuvred themselves into a dead end" when it came to finding a solution to the war, and Tuesday's call was an effort to establish a channel for dialogue.
He drew attention to remarks by Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov on Sunday suggesting Europe should be part of discussions. "I interpret this as a shift in Russia's position, given that Moscow had previously consistently rejected the ⁠idea of discussing a settlement of the war in Ukraine with the Europeans," Mangott said.
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said the call had been coordinated with Kyiv and was "the right approach".
"We welcome such active support for our diplomatic efforts and peace process," he said, adding that he also hoped a local ceasefire around the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky could "pave the way to other steps in the peace process."
But Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said she saw no signs that Russia wanted peace, adding: "I think Europe should stick together rather than going solo."
Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson said other European leaders were not informed of the talks . "My impression is that everyone wants peace, except for Putin himself. I have quite low expectations for this type of conversation," Kristersson told Swedish daily DN.
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said he had told Stubb and Stoere that "absolute caution and vigilance are necessary in such contacts".
Stubb and Stoere said they acted as leaders of their respective countries and not on ‌behalf of Europe, and had "consulted thoroughly with all our partners."
Russia has frequently accused European governments of stoking the war by arming Ukraine and refusing direct talks. A source close to the Kremlin said French President Emmanuel Macron had been the last EU leader to speak with Putin — in a summer call that yielded no results and was not ‌made public.
The source said Putin told Stubb and Stoere that the European involvement was `welcome and that the war needed to end "taking into account the realities on the ground".
Asked what this meant, the person said it signified that Russia would not compromise ⁠over its aim to capture the whole of Ukraine's Donbas region. The Europeans responded by saying a "just" peace was needed, the source said.
The two Nordic leaders may be less encumbered than their peers from larger European states such as Britain, France and Germany, whose ties with Moscow have deteriorated further.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said attempts to end the war "can never find solutions without Ukraine", and must include European countries.
Merz said Germany and other European states wanted to establish a format to speak to Russia's government and that Norway and Finland were playing "a very constructive role" in that effort. The Kremlin said Putin, Stoere and Stubb would keep in touch by phone.

articles.title_orig: Israel election: Israeli exit polls suggest no clear winner with Eisenkot's bloc just ahead of Netanyahu
articles.title_zh: Israel election: Israeli exit polls suggest no clear winner with Eisenkot's bloc just ahead of Netanyahu
articles.content_orig:

Israel 's election ended ⁠in an apparent deadlock on ⁠Tuesday, ​exit ⁠polls ⁠by major ​television networks ⁠showed, ‌with neither prime minister ‌ Benjamin Netanyahu nor ‌his main ⁠rival Gadi Eisenkot on track for a ‌majority.
An inconclusive result would leave Israel in political limbo after the country’s first national election since the October attack in 2023. The vote served as a referendum on Netanyahu’s wartime leadership.
Exit polls released by major Israeli TV stations suggest that neither Netanyahu’s political bloc nor that of his main rival, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, secured the 61 seats needed for a parliamentary majority.
Those polls indicated that Netanyahu's bloc won 50 seats, the opposition won 52-53 and Arab parties won 17-18. The strong showing by Arab-led parties could allow them to decide the next prime minister, but both blocs have until now refused to partner with them.
Netanyahu had been tipped for a stunning defeat in today’s legislative elections despite receiving a glowing endorsement from Donald Trump .
Before polls opened, the US president reiterated his “complete and total” support for Netanyahu, writing that he had been “strong, brave and brilliant in the face of tremendous opposition”.
Former army chief Gadi Eisenkot is a straight talker, media-shy and a relative newcomer to Israeli politics.
He has emerged as a key challenger to Benjamin Netanyahu.
Israel ’s election has ended in a deadlock as no party is on track for majority of the Knesset , exit polls have suggested.
The stalemate comes after three years of war waged in Gaza , Lebanon and Iran , which have plunged the Middle East into turmoil.
The election is widely seen as a referendum on Benjamin Netanyahu , who is seeking another term after a combined 19 years in power .
Benjamin Netanyahu had warned earlier that Arab parties that could make or break the election, saying they were receiving “truly massive support," and heading to the polls in "unprecedented numbers.”
In another sign of concern, Netanyahu’s right-wing Likud party petitioned to extend voting hours past 10 p.m., but the election commission ruled against it, saying there was no justification.
Eisenkot had rejected the proposed extension and called on voters to ignore Netanyahu's “scare tactics.”
Israel's Arab-led parties could emerge as kingmakers — if other parties agree to join forces with them.
“Our vote will change the government,” said Mansour Abbas, head of the Islamist Ra’am party, while voting was still underway.
Arabs in Israel make up about 20% of the population.
Israel’s far-right national security minister, Itamar Ben-Gvir, known for taunting Palestinian detainees and saying some Palestinians in Gaza are “not even people,” warned that “it will be Mansour Abbas’ government” if Netanyahu and his allies don’t win.
Current opposition head Yair Lapid said in a statement: “Don’t let anyone confuse you: the Netanyahu bloc has suffered a crushing defeat. This is a total collapse and the public has told them to go home.”
More than 74% of eligible voters had cast ballots by 8 pm, the highest turnout at that time in decades, and eight percentage points higher than in the last elections in 2022, according to the Central Elections Committee.
Over 7 million people are eligible to vote, and tens of thousands have reportedly arrived from overseas.
Israel’s president will be tasked with asking the party leader with the best prospect of forming a government, usually one with the most seats, to cobble together a coalition.
If none can, new elections could be held early next year.
Israel held five elections between April 2019 and November 2022 because of a similar stalemate.
Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the opposition bloc’s Yashar party, said the projections indicate “a total lack of confidence in Netanyahu and the ‘October 7th government’”.
The stalemate in today’s election could work in Benjamin Netanyahu's favour, allowing the prime minister to remain in power in a caretaker capacity while parties try to forge a governing coalition.
Final results could take days, and Israel's fragmented political system leaves smaller parties potential kingmakers.
No single party has ever won 61 seats outright in the 120-seat Knesset, making coalitions the norm.

articles.title_orig: Israel's election has a high turnout, lifting opposition hopes of beating Netanyahu
articles.title_zh: Israel's election has a high turnout, lifting opposition hopes of beating Netanyahu
articles.content_orig:
A video wall displays images of Benjamin Netanyahu with President Trump at a Likud party event before the release of the first exit poll results in Israel's general election, in Jerusalem, on Tuesday. David Goldman/AP hide caption
Israeli voters turned out in their highest numbers in decades in a tense national election on Tuesday to decide whether to stick with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's far-right coalition or change course.
Netanyahu is in a tight race with his top rival, Gadi Eisenkot, a center-right former military chief of staff, according to early exit polls after voting ended at 10 p.m. local time. The preliminary results broadcast across Israeli TV networks didn't show a clear winner, but appeared to give the opposition bloc of parties led by Eisenkot a slight edge over Netanyahu's governing coalition.
Still, the final vote count may not be known until Wednesday. And even then, if no bloc wins an outright majority, it may take days or weeks to find who will be Israel's next prime minister as party leaders try to assemble a governing coalition.
Israelis consider this one of their most consequential votes in history — the first parliamentary election since the October 2023 Hamas-led attack and the start of wars in Gaza and elsewhere in the Middle East.
The early exit polls suggested Netanyahu's Likud Party won the most seats, with Eisenkot's Yashar party coming second, but no party won an outright majority in the 120-seat parliament, known as the Knesset.
The final results will depend on the math and negotiations among broader alliances. The bloc of four opposition parties led by Eisenkot appeared to win a combined 52 seats, over the Netanyahu coalition's 50, according to three major exit polls.
Opposition leaders quickly reacted to the preliminary results, saying they suggested voters dealt a blow to Netanyahu's coalition .
Shira Efron, an analyst at the Rand Corp. think tank, agreed that it could be an opposition victory.
"This is a very good outcome for Eisenkot" and his recently formed party, Efron told NPR. "The most likely scenario is that he will receive the mandate from the president to form the government," she told NPR. She said he could try to form a minority government or join an alliance with Arab politicians.
Enthusiasm was especially high among voters seeking to replace Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister, with almost two decades in office across multiple tenures.
" Important is an underestimation, because it's much more than important. It's crucial," voter Naama Aaronsohn said of the election. "I'm worried. ... What's going to become of our country if there's not a major change?"
Another voter, Itamar Ariel, said there are problems in Israel but no one can replace Netanyahu. He said his choice is about security for Israel.
Netanyahu voiced alarm throughout the day, in a number of social media posts, commenting on the high number of Arab citizens of Israel who were turning up at the polls. Netanyahu urged his right-wing supporters to vote.
Nur Abu Na, a 30-year-old nurse, called Netanyahu's government racist against Arab citizens and said she believes it's important for the her Arab community to vote. There are two predominantly Arab parties in the elections.
"This government it's not good for us and ... not good for anyone," she said.
President Trump publicly endorsed Netanyahu . After going to war together against Iran, in June 2025 and again this February, the two leaders plan to launch major attacks against Iran after the Israeli and U.S. midterm elections.
This is a developing story and may be updated.
Daniel Estrin reported from Tel Aviv, Israel. Ruth Sherlock reported from Jerusalem. Samantha Balaban, Itay Stern, Shir David and Alon Avital contributed reporting in Israel.
NPR does not offer or accept money for coverage or interviews. Anyone who makes such an offer or request is not an NPR employee and does not represent NPR.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia, AMD Get Their Jollies Hooking Up With Meta's Muse
articles.title_zh: Nvidia, AMD Get Their Jollies Hooking Up With Meta's Muse
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices have said they will invest a total of $4 billion in Meta after the social media and artificial intelligence giant announced plans to raise $95 billion to support its investments in AI infrastructure.
Meta on Monday said it would initially raise $35 billion in underwritten public equity offerings, before raising an additional $60 billion with an at-the-market program.
Nvidia on Tuesday said it would invest $3 billion in Meta's equity offering, with AMD announcing it would invest $1 billion.
Meta's Monday announcement said Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom were interested in purchasing up to $5 billion in shares.
Nvidia announced its investment on Tuesday, adding that Meta would expand Vera Rubin and Vera CPU deployment, and that the two companies would deepen their partnership on Muse, the social media giant's AI agent that launched last month.
"AI agents represent a new computing paradigm — software that understands our goals, reasons, uses tools and gets work done on our behalf," said Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang in a statement.
"This changes how we use computers, from operating applications to working with intelligent agents."
"We're excited to keep working with NVIDIA to deliver the best personal agents and frontier models for billions of people," said Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg.
AMD said that its Helios racks were running at Meta and its EPYC processors were powering Meta's Muse.
"Together, we are building and deploying infrastructure at gigawatt scale and shaping future generations of silicon, software and systems to enable Meta's most ambitious superintelligence models and services," AMD CEO Lisa Su said in a statement.
AMD was up 3% on Tuesday, while Nvidia stayed flat. Meta was down 1%.
Nvidia and AMD have been rapidly building up stakes in companies powering the AI boom.
Nvidia has invested in OpenAI, Anthropic, Intel and XAI and participated in 121 investment rounds so far this year, according to Dealroom, up from just 13 in 2022.
AMD in July said it would make an equity investment of up to $5 billion in Anthropic. The company has been involved in 25 funding rounds in 2026, up from just two in 2022.

articles.title_orig: Anthropic IPO warns its AI could blackmail people, become sentient, end humanity
articles.title_zh: Anthropic IPO warns its AI could blackmail people, become sentient, end humanity
articles.content_orig:
The tech industry needs this to go well. So does Wall Street.
Anthropic's IPO filing on Monday puts the Claude creator in position to pursue what could be the largest initial stock offering in history. Investors are already measuring the 5-year-old company's potential market cap in the trillions, putting it in a category with the world's most valuable companies.
It's a critical moment for the whole tech sector, as the artificial intelligence boom has been largely driven by two companies: Anthropic and OpenAI. The latter has confidentially filed to go public, but has said a debut likely won't take place until 2027.
Meanwhile, the stock market is showing signs of jitters on the AI trade. Neoclouds and data center companies have been getting pummeled, prompting Australia's Firmus to withdraw its IPO plans and for SK Hynix's U.S.-based Solidigm unit to do the same.
Now, all eyes turn to Anthropic , which is betting that investors will look past over $80 billion in losses in the first half of the year, and see the 14-fold increase in revenue as a reflection of seemingly insatiable demand for the company's leading models and services.
"If it underperforms expectations, it'll be a little bit of a house of cards," said Jai Das, co-founder of Sapphire Ventures whose career in tech investing dates to the 1990s.
Anthropic's business is deeply entwined with tech megacaps. Close to half its revenue comes from Claude being sold through cloud divisions at Microsoft , Amazon and Alphabet , which all hold investments in the company. In the IPO, some $77 billion in notes can be issued to Amazon , Broadcom and Google , while Microsoft and Nvidia agreed to invest $15 billion as the company builds up its computing capacity. Chips from Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices , Amazon and Google are powering Anthropic's development.
Cloud providers are ratcheting up capital expenditures to meet demand, and memory manufacturers are fighting shortages to prioritize AI chips. And there's the debt factor. Alphabet, with its investment-grade credit rating, committed to backstopping Anthropic for a data center in Texas. Broadcom , which helps Google develop chips for AI labs, is creating financing pools to help Anthropic and OpenAI deploy high-performance models, CEO Hock Tan told analysts earlier this year.
For public market investors, more than one-third of the value of the S&P 500 comes from tech's trillion-dollar companies, which are all, to varying degrees, going deep in AI. Beyond that, there are software giants like Adobe and Salesforce that have integrated with Anthropic's Claude assistant.
And in the private markets, check sizes have ballooned but IPOs are few and far between. Bessemer Venture Partners and Menlo Ventures both told CNBC that Anthropic is their biggest investment ever.
"If they don't perform well, they will become the bellwether for AI," said Brad Bernstein, a managing partner at growth equity firm FTV Capital. "Their valuation will reflect that performance variation, and then it'll just be a trickle-down effect to all the stuff going on with the excess capital that's getting poured into the venture AI world. Everything is going to have to sort of be reset."
Anthropic will be the third company to go public with a valuation above $1 trillion, after Saudi Aramco and Elon Musk's SpaceX , which debuted in June. OpenAI could be the fourth.
Revenue at Anthropic has been multiplying at a staggering pace as businesses adopt the company's coding and productivity tools. Second-quarter revenue soared to $11.56 billion from $787 million a year earlier.
The company held almost $132 billion in cash, equivalents and short-term investments at the end of June. And after five quarters of operating losses, Anthropic reported $974 million in operating income for the second quarter.
"It is, I think, better than feared," said Rohit Kulkarni, partner and chief AI officer at Burnham Park Capital Markets, referring to the financials. "There could have been more negative tidbits."
One source of concern in some corners of the investing universe is the emergence of so-called open-weight models, which are cheaper for businesses to access and allow for customization and flexibility in terms of where users access the models.
In the prospectus, the only two competitors Anthropic named were OpenAI and Google, though the company said it faces competition from a "broader set of model providers," including open-weight or open-source models.
Anthropic says it's all very early, with Fortune 500 companies committing less than 0.1% of their total expenses to its models and services in the latest quarter. Michael Monaghan, portfolio manager at Founder ETFs, says that's part of the investment thesis.
"I think there's going to be room for frontier models like Anthropic and OpenAI and SpaceX, and I think there will be room for open-weight models," Monaghan said. "It's way too soon to say that one is going to disintermediate the other."
With hyperscaler spending on AI infrastructure set to reach into the trillions of dollars, Sapphire's Das said there's understandable concern about a market glut. But he compares it to the telecommunications and dot-com bubble of the late 1990s, when companies flooded the market with fiber-optic equipment. Eventually, the infrastructure got used, although plenty of companies went belly up in the interim.
"Long term, I don't think there is a lack of demand," Das said.
A lackluster debut could push out OpenAI's offering even further and cause investors to rethink its lofty valuation. At the same time, rising interest rates mean it's getting costlier for companies to raise debt.
David Trainer, CEO of financial research firm New Constructs, wrote in a report last month that the AI boom has been built on the view that cheap credit and access to the capital markets will be "readily available."
"If AI liquidity dries up, and there are clear signs it is, we see large, 20%, downside risk in the S&P 500, with most of that concentrated in the valuation of AI-related stocks," Trainer wrote.
Industry experts take a different approach, focusing on the power and rapid proliferation of the technology. Claude Opus 5.5 Max performs better than any other model on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, an industry benchmark .
Snowflake CEO Sridhar Ramaswamy said the technology is only becoming more essential.
"Anthropic and OpenAI have by now demonstrated their ability to stay at the frontier of AI and keep pushing innovation," Ramaswamy said. "They're incredible companies that are doing a big service to humanity by expanding the frontier of what is possible, and we are very much rooting for them to be public and very successful companies."
Still, Snowflake is experimenting with low-cost open-weight models from China's Moonshot AI, DeepSeek and Zhipu.
"We spend a lot on internal AI because we want to get as much efficiency as we can," Ramaswamy said.

articles.title_orig: DIA Releases Clearest Image of China’s Reusable Spaceplane with Service Module Attached
articles.title_zh: DIA Releases Clearest Image of China’s Reusable Spaceplane with Service Module Attached
articles.content_orig:
The U.S. Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) has released a new image of China’s secretive reusable spaceplane, captured by a Maxar Technologies spacecraft in 2024. Published in the DIA’s “Challenges to Security in Space” report on Oct. 26, 2026, the photo provides a rare view of the spacecraft in orbit with its service module attached.
China’s reusable experimental spacecraft has flown four orbital missions since September 2020, launched aboard Long March 2F rockets. The first mission lasted two days; the second, launched in August 2022, remained in orbit for 276 days; and the third, launched in December 2023, lasted 268 days. A fourth mission began in February 2026.
Before the release of the Maxar image, public imagery was limited to grainy ground-based telescope observations and computer-generated illustrations with Chinese markings. Space tracking forums in early 2023 observed the Chinese spacecraft connecting with another object multiple times, but no image existed at the time.
The Maxar image used in the DIA report is dated to 2024, when the spacecraft launched in December 2023 was still in orbit during its third mission. The timing is therefore consistent with the photograph depicting the vehicle during that flight, although the exact date of capture has not been publicly disclosed.
Behold: The US Defense Intelligence Agency has released a report on challenges to security in space, including an NEI image of China’s spaceplane from Maxar, taken in 2024. https://t.co/F3msSwoFph
— Andrew Jones (@AJ_FI) October 27, 2026
The report identifies two Chinese space models, Shenlong and Tengyun, but it is not known which of those is in the image. The Chinese spacecraft is often compared with the U.S. Space Force’s X-37B because both are uncrewed reusable orbital vehicles designed to return to Earth.
However, the Chinese vehicle’s design, payload, and mission objectives remain largely undisclosed. Tracking data indicate that it has deployed objects and performed rendezvous and proximity operations, but these observations do not establish the spacecraft’s intended military role.
The spaceplane appears in the DIA’s broader assessment of space-related capabilities and threats, whose goal is to cover the capabilities of strategic rivals. “The updated report details the space defense and military goals, including strategies, plans and intentions, of China, Russia and the emerging space powers of Iran and North Korea,” says the press release .
The image provides a view of the underside of China’s reusable spaceplane, with its service module attached and solar arrays deployed. The module is understood to provide electrical power and propulsion during the orbital mission before separating from the spaceplane ahead of reentry, similarly to the X-37B’s service module.
The image also appears to show the spacecraft’s payload-bay doors, although the precise configuration and function of the visible features have not been publicly detailed. Among the possibilities are systems like robotic arms, small satellites or specimens for in-orbit testing.
Now then — this could be something exceptional. The rumours are that inside this exceptional payload fairing atop a CZ-2F is a CASC spaceplane, launching from Jiuquan Friday. Source: 俊了个锅 via 林晓弈。 https://t.co/qs6VRfzQoP https://t.co/ZPnpwAIfyO
— Andrew Jones (@AJ_FI) September 3, 2020
Beijing launched its first ever reusable spaceplane prototype on Sep. 4, 2020 aboard a Long March 2F carrier rocket from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwestern China’s Gobi desert. The spacecraft remained in orbit for two days before returning to Earth.
Although Chinese authorities did not initially disclose the landing site in detail, open-source analysis of satellite imagery associated the landing with a runway near the Lop Nur nuclear test site in northwestern China.
Since its launch on 4 August 2022, we observed multiple large maneuvers raising the object’s altitude — as well as repeated deployments, formation flying, and docking of a sub-satellite Object J (NORAD ID 54218). https://t.co/ORVgSXYKmJ
— LeoLabs (@LeoLabs_Space) May 8, 2023
The second launch of the space plane took place on Aug. 4, 2022, this time spending 276 days in orbit until May 8, 2023. According to the DIA, the vehicle appeared to “maneuver with a companion satellite and conduct station-keeping at around 1 km separation.”
“At one point, the two objects appeared within 100 meters of one another. The spaceplane and satellite possibly rendezvoused before the satellite was re-released,” the DIA report said.
This event tested our object tracking and maneuver detection and characterization capabilities, proving that we can provide critical intelligence on the behaviors and activities of objects in #LEO thanks to our continuous, real-time operations. https://t.co/WDP06ffBSv
— LeoLabs (@LeoLabs_Space) May 8, 2023
On May 8, 2023, commercial space-tracking company LeoLabs reported that its observations indicated repeated deployments, formation flying, and apparent docking or capture operations involving ‘Object J’:
“Since its launch on 4 August 2022, we observed multiple large maneuvers raising the object’s altitude – as well as repeated deployments, formation flying, and docking of a sub-satellite Object J (NORAD ID 54218). We’ve determined that the Test Spacecraft2 has propulsive capability and engaged in proximity operations with Object J, including what appeared to be at least two and possibly three capture/docking operations.”
China launched the spacecraft on its third orbital mission on Dec. 14, 2023. It remained in orbit for 268 days, returning on Sept. 6, 2024, according to the DIA report.
During that flight, the spacecraft again “released and interacted with an object,”according to the DIA. Considering that the Maxar image was captured in 2024, we can presume the vehicle was photographed during this third mission.
Although this was not covered by the report, the spacecraft’s fourth mission began in February 2026. Orbital-tracking data analyzed by astronomer Jonathan McDowell indicated that the vehicle released and subsequently recaptured the same object, whose precise identity and purpose remain unknown, with similar operations reportedly repeated later in the flight.
then executed a rerendezvous with the subsat on Sep 10 and a recapture on Sep  13. This analysis is based on USSF GP data. USSF also cataloged an additional object 24J on about Sep 10, but with no orbit data; I think this was a mistake and is a duplicate of object 24H.
— Jonathan McDowell (@planet4589) September 23, 2026
The spacecraft’s proximity operations have raised questions about potential counterspace applications, with some theories assigning more exotic kinetic ‘anti-satellite’ capabilities to the Chinese spacecraft.
While there is no evidence yet the vehicle is designed as a kinetic anti-satellite weapon, and the spaceplane’s intended mission remains undisclosed, space is becoming a contested domain. The observed rendezvous and capture capabilities can support satellite inspection and servicing, but could also enable interference with other spacecraft.
The spacecraft’s potential military applications remain uncertain. While there is no public evidence confirming that the vehicle carries military payloads, such a platform could be used for space-based reconnaissance, intelligence-gathering, and monitoring of other space objects, as well as kinetic missions possibly involving the use of directed energy weapons, offensive weapons or electronic warfare.

US District Judge Eumi K. Lee ruled on Monday that the government had failed to provide sufficient evidence to justify the restriction, which effectively forces lobbying firms to choose between representing Alibaba and clients seeking Pentagon contracts.

articles.title_orig: European Leaders Split Over Phone Call to Putin
articles.title_zh: European Leaders Split Over Phone Call to Putin
articles.content_orig:
The leaders of Finland and Norway have held a joint call with Vladimir Putin - rare contact between the Russian president and European leaders.
Finland's President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre said the aim of the call had been to "convey messages directly regarding future negotiations" towards peace. An end to the conflict in Ukraine "will not be achieved through silence," Stubb said.
Neither side suggested the needle had been moved on ending the war, which began when Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
Although the Finnish leader said the conversation with Putin had been "frank and substantive," Støre added that there were "big differences in views" with Putin.
Several European leaders have recently shown willingness to engage with Russia directly, but both Stubb and Støre pointed out their initiative was taken in their capacity as neighbours of Russia, rather than on behalf of Europe as a whole.
"We've not set out to speak on behalf of anyone other than ourselves," Støre said.
Stubb added the call had been prepared in consultation with Ukraine and the US following a meeting between Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, the Nordic leaders and US special envoy Steve Witkoff in Oslo last week.
The first trilateral US-Ukraine-Russia talks since the start of the year are tentatively planned for early November in Abu Dhabi.
Zelensky later confirmed Stubb and Støre debriefed him after the call and said he was grateful for their "active support", while his Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said the call had been "the right approach".
Finland and Norway, which border Russia, initiated the 90-minute call - held from Helsinki - to "discuss Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine and the diplomatic efforts to end the war and promote peace and stability in Europe", the leaders' offices said.
Støre added: "The war comes with enormous human and material costs... The suffering and destruction will impact generations."
The Kremlin said Putin told the leaders that "a just and lasting peace" would only be possible if Russia's interests were considered.
Putin also reaffirmed to the Nordic leaders what he views as the "root causes" of the conflict - his frequent shorthand for Ukraine's desire to exist as a sovereign state.
"A fair long-term peace settlement is possible only if Russia's legal interests are taken into account fully and unconditionally", Putin said.
All three parties reportedly agreed to continue their direct phone communication.
There was no official EU reaction to the talks. The dialogue had not been coordinated with other European leaders, the Danish and Swedish prime ministers said. "I think Europe should stick together rather than going solo," commented Sweden's Ulf Kristersson.
Meanwhile, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Stubb had informed him that Europe's position on the upcoming talks in the United Arab Emirates was "moderately optimistic".
Relations between the US and Ukraine and its European allies have soured since US President Donald Trump agreed to lift some sanctions from Russia, allowing Moscow to export oil to the America.
As the Trump administration's position on Russia has softened, several European leaders have said Europe should be trying to re-establish direct contacts with the Kremlin.
Stubb and Støre are the first European leaders to contact Putin since French President Emmanuel Macron's conversation with him in July 2025.
Soon after, Putin visited Alaska for a summit with Trump, and from then on Europeans were further sidelined from Ukraine peace talks. Moscow regularly mocks European leaders and accuses the EU of prolonging the war by supplying Ukraine with weapons.
But last weekend, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said having a European negotiator at the peace talks table would be "good".
And although he said Moscow did not view Finland and Norway as speaking on behalf of Europe, on Tuesday Peskov conceded that Stubb and Støre's talks with Putin had been "very constructive and practical talks with the leaders of two key neighbouring states."

Apple reportedly plans to introduce a low-cost iPhone 18e next spring alongside iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2. Here are the details on what to expect from iPhone 18e, per a new leak.
When Apple introduced new iPhones last month, only three models launched: iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, plus iPhone Duo.
Rumors indicate three more new iPhones are coming in early 2027: iPhone 18e, iPhone 18, and iPhone Air 2.
There’s been plenty of reporting on iPhone Air 2 changes , and some on the base iPhone 18 , but surprisingly little on the entry-model iPhone 18e.
But today, a new post from Weibo leaker Digital Chat Station outlines what to expect from iPhone 18e early next year. He says it will feature:
Based on these specs, it sounds like iPhone 18e is focused largely on performance improvements.
The A20 chip will be interesting to evaluate, since we haven’t yet seen a non-Pro variant of the latest 2nm technology. Mention of a front camera upgrade is particularly surprising, but my guess is that if it does emerge, it will actually be an 18MP sensor like what’s in other models today.
Other than these two changes, every spec mentioned remains unchanged from iPhone 17e. One detail not addressed is whether the notch will be replaced by a Dynamic Island.
Considering the skyrocketing prices of memory and storage, and Apple’s aims to keep iPhone 18e a budget-friendly model, perhaps the new model will offer fewer upgrades than usual to keep costs down.

articles.title_orig: Code-execution flaw in UEFI firmware threatens most servers on planet Earth
articles.title_zh: Code-execution flaw in UEFI firmware threatens most servers on planet Earth
articles.content_orig:
Defenders across the world face the burden of responding to yet another botched code-execution vulnerability, this time in boot-time firmware used by most of the world’s server vendors and data centers.
The vulnerability, with a severity rating of 9.5 out of 10, resides in the TianoCore EDK II , an open source codebase that hardware makers and cloud providers use to create the UEFI firmware that runs during the boot-up sequence. Last year, a representative of the UEFI Forum called EDK2 the “preeminent solution / implementation of the UEFI specifications.” Virtually all UEFI suppliers (sometimes still called IBVs or independent BIOS vendors), including AMI, Insyde, and Phoenix, use the reference code extensively. Project Mu, Microsoft’s hardened EDK2 fork, used the code containing the vulnerable component as well.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-97631, is a memory-corruption flaw in an ICMP component that attackers can exploit to execute malicious code that runs before the operating system and firmware can implement defenses like Secure Boot , which establishes a chain of trust for all code, including the Trusted Platform Module (TPM), loaded during boot. While final payloads delivered by CVE-2026-97631 have no persistence—meaning they run only once—they can give attackers a wide opening to install other payloads that also run each time early in the boot process.
The parties that discovered CVE-2026-97631—Alex Matrosov of Anthropic and Dan Holmes of Google—had arranged for it to stay under wraps until a coordinated disclosure that was scheduled for January. AMI, a maker of motherboards and other hardware, published this pull request last month that detailed the vulnerability and included a code fix. Once the post came to the attention of the discovering parties, TianoCore Project members published a public advisory last week.
With publicly available patch code, it will be trivial for advanced hackers to learn how the vulnerability is triggered and to build working exploits. Further compounding the urgency, patching UEFI code vulnerabilities in millions of end devices sold and used by thousands of hardware makers and cloud providers is cumbersome and time-consuming. Word of the vulnerability comes six days after another botched disclosure, this one involving a critical code-execution vulnerability in the PHP programming language.
“This vulnerability in the ICMP parser of the EDK2 network stack is interesting in terms of how it affects the chain of trust and the broader ecosystem,” said HD Moore, creator of Metasploit and chief research officer at security firm Dragos. “An attacker intent on compromising a nearby endpoint or server could use this bug to hijack program flow at a point where the boot process still has access to sensitive components, like the endpoint’s TPM. This could be used to break disk encryption for cases where an attacker has short-term network access (and it would be even easier in a theft scenario).”
CVE-2026-97631 is a 16-year-old buffer overflow in the PXE-Base Code driver (NetworkPkg/UefiPxeBcDxe), which is responsible for allowing servers, storage equipment, and other devices to boot using code downloaded from a local network. During this process—known as the pre-execution environment boot—the driver uses a network listener to monitor for ICMP errors. Because the driver doesn’t enforce a memory copy limit of 504 bytes, overwriting adjacent data, a malicious insider or a hacker who has gained low-level access to a local network can send an error message that appends code past this limit. The IUEFI module running on the CPU then becomes corrupted.
As the official advisory puts it:
During network boot, the PXE Base Code driver (NetworkPkg/UefiPxeBcDxe) keeps a receive request open for ICMP error messages and copies each received message into the fixed 504-byte field Mode.IcmpError of its private context structure. The copy loop’s bounds handling is incorrect in both the IPv4 and IPv6 handlers (PxeBcIcmpErrorDpcHandle and PxeBcIcmp6ErrorDpcHandle): for a message longer than 504 bytes it still copies bytes into the field, and it advances the destination pointer by the cumulative rather than the per-fragment length, so an oversized message writes attacker-controlled bytes past the field. Nothing earlier on the receive path restricts the message length.
The malicious error can be delivered through a simple unicast sent from any network distance to a target device’s IP address, as long as it’s sent during the PXE boot sequence. An attacker can deliver a denial-of-service by causing the boot sequence to hang. When the attacker knows what the target firmware build is, it can plant a “counterfeit event” that executes the malicious code on the CPU in its UEFI firmware environment. The code runs in ring 0, a CPU’s most privileged execution level. Because exploits bypass attestation processes designed to cryptographically prove to remote servers that the hardware is secure, they present a key opportunity for elevating limited privileges.
CVE-2026-97631 joins a long list of previously discovered vulnerabilities in UEFI or code that works closely with it. The most severe of them, LogoFail , stemmed from logo images included in the UEFI of just about every hardware maker. Rendering bugs allowed attackers to subvert the chain of trust UEFI enforces and go on to install malicious components before the OS loaded or Secure Boot ran. PixieFail was a vulnerability similar to CVE-2026-97631. It, too, was the result of faulty PXE boot flaws in EDK2. Following discovery of the vulnerability, researchers embarked on multiple fuzzing projects designed to surface other critical flaws in the open source code library. It appears those efforts failed to find this latest flaw.
Other recently discovered UEFI flaws include:
Like CVE-2026-97631, exploitation or use of these payloads is appealing because it allows attackers to infect machines early in the boot process, before TPM and other defenses load, so they can inflict maximum damage. Given the ubiquity of CVE-2026-97631, Moore said it’s likely a “forever” bug that will live on in end-of-support systems.
There are important caveats and limitations to exploiting this latest vulnerability. As noted, some level of control over a local network is a prerequisite. That likely limits exploitation to insiders or attackers, such as nation-states or ransomware operators, who manage to gain low-level access inside a network and are looking for a way to elevate system rights. There’s no evidence yet that CVE-2026-97631 provides an initial entry point into a network. There are other hurdles to clear.
“For exploiting the vulnerability itself, an attacker needs to guess specific addresses within the target system, so it’s not something that you can throw a single exploit at any target and get RCE across a diverse range of devices, but it needs to be tuned for each target model/version/configuration since the addresses will change based on those,” Jesse Michael, a principal researcher at firmware security firm Eclypsium, told Ars. “Unlike some of the previous, high-profile vulnerabilities like BootHole, Black Lotus, and Baton Drop, this vulnerability can be fixed with a basic code fix, which will require deploying a BIOS/UEFI update, but they don’t need to deal with revocations, pk/kek/db/dbx key management updates, or making sure to update OS and provisioning media like you do with Secure Boot bypasses in the bootloader itself.”
CVE-2026-97631 doesn’t affect home and small office users, or any other users who boot their devices solely from disk drives. Instead, it applies only to organizations with machines that boot from local networks, or conceivably from Internet-connected resources. Even then, the targeted firmware must rely on EDK2, as opposed to a different reference implementation, and use the PXE functionality (which is turned on by default).

articles.title_orig: Wall Street ends higher on revived AI momentum
articles.title_zh: Wall Street ends higher on revived AI momentum
articles.content_orig:
The tech industry needs this to go well. So does Wall Street.
Anthropic's IPO filing on Monday puts the Claude creator in position to pursue what could be the largest initial stock offering in history. Investors are already measuring the 5-year-old company's potential market cap in the trillions, putting it in a category with the world's most valuable companies.
It's a critical moment for the whole tech sector, as the artificial intelligence boom has been largely driven by two companies: Anthropic and OpenAI. The latter has confidentially filed to go public, but has said a debut likely won't take place until 2027.
Meanwhile, the stock market is showing signs of jitters on the AI trade. Neoclouds and data center companies have been getting pummeled, prompting Australia's Firmus to withdraw its IPO plans and for SK Hynix's U.S.-based Solidigm unit to do the same.
Now, all eyes turn to Anthropic , which is betting that investors will look past over $80 billion in losses in the first half of the year, and see the 14-fold increase in revenue as a reflection of seemingly insatiable demand for the company's leading models and services.
"If it underperforms expectations, it'll be a little bit of a house of cards," said Jai Das, co-founder of Sapphire Ventures whose career in tech investing dates to the 1990s.
Anthropic's business is deeply entwined with tech megacaps. Close to half its revenue comes from Claude being sold through cloud divisions at Microsoft , Amazon and Alphabet , which all hold investments in the company. In the IPO, some $77 billion in notes can be issued to Amazon , Broadcom and Google , while Microsoft and Nvidia agreed to invest $15 billion as the company builds up its computing capacity. Chips from Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices , Amazon and Google are powering Anthropic's development.
Cloud providers are ratcheting up capital expenditures to meet demand, and memory manufacturers are fighting shortages to prioritize AI chips. And there's the debt factor. Alphabet, with its investment-grade credit rating, committed to backstopping Anthropic for a data center in Texas. Broadcom , which helps Google develop chips for AI labs, is creating financing pools to help Anthropic and OpenAI deploy high-performance models, CEO Hock Tan told analysts earlier this year.
For public market investors, more than one-third of the value of the S&P 500 comes from tech's trillion-dollar companies, which are all, to varying degrees, going deep in AI. Beyond that, there are software giants like Adobe and Salesforce that have integrated with Anthropic's Claude assistant.
And in the private markets, check sizes have ballooned but IPOs are few and far between. Bessemer Venture Partners and Menlo Ventures both told CNBC that Anthropic is their biggest investment ever.
"If they don't perform well, they will become the bellwether for AI," said Brad Bernstein, a managing partner at growth equity firm FTV Capital. "Their valuation will reflect that performance variation, and then it'll just be a trickle-down effect to all the stuff going on with the excess capital that's getting poured into the venture AI world. Everything is going to have to sort of be reset."
Anthropic will be the third company to go public with a valuation above $1 trillion, after Saudi Aramco and Elon Musk's SpaceX , which debuted in June. OpenAI could be the fourth.
Revenue at Anthropic has been multiplying at a staggering pace as businesses adopt the company's coding and productivity tools. Second-quarter revenue soared to $11.56 billion from $787 million a year earlier.
The company held almost $132 billion in cash, equivalents and short-term investments at the end of June. And after five quarters of operating losses, Anthropic reported $974 million in operating income for the second quarter.
"It is, I think, better than feared," said Rohit Kulkarni, partner and chief AI officer at Burnham Park Capital Markets, referring to the financials. "There could have been more negative tidbits."
One source of concern in some corners of the investing universe is the emergence of so-called open-weight models, which are cheaper for businesses to access and allow for customization and flexibility in terms of where users access the models.
In the prospectus, the only two competitors Anthropic named were OpenAI and Google, though the company said it faces competition from a "broader set of model providers," including open-weight or open-source models.
Anthropic says it's all very early, with Fortune 500 companies committing less than 0.1% of their total expenses to its models and services in the latest quarter. Michael Monaghan, portfolio manager at Founder ETFs, says that's part of the investment thesis.
"I think there's going to be room for frontier models like Anthropic and OpenAI and SpaceX, and I think there will be room for open-weight models," Monaghan said. "It's way too soon to say that one is going to disintermediate the other."
With hyperscaler spending on AI infrastructure set to reach into the trillions of dollars, Sapphire's Das said there's understandable concern about a market glut. But he compares it to the telecommunications and dot-com bubble of the late 1990s, when companies flooded the market with fiber-optic equipment. Eventually, the infrastructure got used, although plenty of companies went belly up in the interim.
"Long term, I don't think there is a lack of demand," Das said.
A lackluster debut could push out OpenAI's offering even further and cause investors to rethink its lofty valuation. At the same time, rising interest rates mean it's getting costlier for companies to raise debt.
David Trainer, CEO of financial research firm New Constructs, wrote in a report last month that the AI boom has been built on the view that cheap credit and access to the capital markets will be "readily available."
"If AI liquidity dries up, and there are clear signs it is, we see large, 20%, downside risk in the S&P 500, with most of that concentrated in the valuation of AI-related stocks," Trainer wrote.
Industry experts take a different approach, focusing on the power and rapid proliferation of the technology. Claude Opus 5.5 Max performs better than any other model on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, an industry benchmark .
Snowflake CEO Sridhar Ramaswamy said the technology is only becoming more essential.
"Anthropic and OpenAI have by now demonstrated their ability to stay at the frontier of AI and keep pushing innovation," Ramaswamy said. "They're incredible companies that are doing a big service to humanity by expanding the frontier of what is possible, and we are very much rooting for them to be public and very successful companies."
Still, Snowflake is experimenting with low-cost open-weight models from China's Moonshot AI, DeepSeek and Zhipu.
"We spend a lot on internal AI because we want to get as much efficiency as we can," Ramaswamy said.

articles.title_zh: Robinhood shares fall 5% as crypto slump weighs on profits, offsetting gains in new businesses
articles.content_orig:
Robinhood shares fell 4% in after-hours trading as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.
Here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept. 30,  compared with Wall Street estimates, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:
Robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago. Revenue represented a 12% increase from $1.27 billion in the same quarter last year.
Despite that gain, transaction-based revenue of $867 million came in below Wall Street estimates from StreetAccount of $879 million, putting the focus on whether Robinhood can sustain momentum across its trading businesses and reduce its reliance on volatile market activity.
Robinhood has been diversifying its business as it tries to expand its brokerage app into a broader financial services platform. Options trading and event contracts have become increasingly important sources of transaction revenue, while the company has continued to invest in wealth management, subscriptions and other offerings.
Transaction-based revenue grew 19% from the same period last year to $867 million, driven primarily by a more than 500% increase in event contracts revenue. Additionally, options revenue grew 31% to $399 million and equities revenue rose 41% to $121 million.
Those gains were partially offset by cryptocurrency revenue, which fell 55% to $120 million.
Chief Financial Officer Shiv Verma told CNBC event contracts on crypto movements did well in the quarter, offering investors another way to express a view on crypto despite the slump in prices and spot trading.
Net deposits on the Robinhood platform totaled $15.7 billion for the quarter, equal to a 17% annualized growth rate based on total platform assets at the end of Q2 2026. Over the past year, net deposits totaled $71 billion, representing 21% growth compared with total platform assets at the end of Q3 2025.
—With reporting from CNBC's Robert Hum and Kate Rooney

articles.title_orig: UPS Stock Jumps After Earnings Deliver Good News for the U.S. Economy
articles.title_zh: UPS Stock Jumps After Earnings Deliver Good News for the U.S. Economy
articles.content_orig:
United Parcel Service on Tuesday reported third-quarter results that beat Wall Street expectations and raised its full-year guidance.
The guidance raise comes after the company already upped its outlook last quarter . UPS now said it's projecting full-year consolidated revenue of approximately $92.6 billion, up from its previous expectations of $91.2 billion, as well as fourth-quarter revenue of $25.7 billion.
Shares of UPS rose slightly in morning trading.
Here's how the company performed in its third quarter, compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:
For the quarter ended Sept. 30, UPS reported net income of $1.16 billion, or $1.37 per share, down slightly from net income of $1.31 billion, or $1.55, the year prior. Adjusting for one-time expenses, UPS reported earnings per share of $1.69. Revenue rose 6.7% to $22.9 billion.
In its domestic segment, the company said it saw a 4.5% increase in revenue, while its international segment had a 7.1% rise in revenue. Its supply chain solutions business saw an 18.2% revenue increase, which UPS said was primarily driven to growth in forwarding and logistics, including healthcare . On a call with analysts, CEO Carol Tomé said healthcare revenue exceeded $3 billion for the third consecutive quarter.
The company had previously said it expected its third-quarter domestic revenue to be flat and for domestic average daily volume to fall due to seasonal declines and the glide down with Amazon .
"We're driving more premium growth, improving revenue quality and mix, and creating greater operating leverage through a more efficient network," Tomé said on the call. "All of this is strengthening the underlying performance of our business."
UPS has been in the midst of a turnaround under Tomé's leadership, working to create a leaner business model and leveraging automation to position the company for growth.
As the company prepares for its peak holiday season, Tomé said the consumer remains resilient, and the growth in average daily volume between the third and fourth quarters will be consistent with last year. However, fourth-quarter domestic average daily volume is expected to fall due to the reduction with Amazon.
She added that nearly 70% of all packages will flow through an automated process this holiday season.

articles.title_orig: SpaceX CEO Elon Musk Just Gave Telecoms Some Great News
articles.title_zh: SpaceX CEO Elon Musk Just Gave Telecoms Some Great News
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
On Monday, Verizon Communications Inc. (NYSE: VZ ) CEO Dan Schulman sees opportunities to collaborate with satellite providers such as Elon Musk's Starlink , but says the wireless carrier has no reason to let Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NASDAQ: SPCX ) use its network to compete for mobile customers .
Speaking during Verizon's third-quarter earnings call, Schulman acknowledged that satellite connectivity could complement traditional wireless services, particularly in remote areas with limited cellular coverage.
"I do think there is a role for satellite for sure in remote areas. It's a great service for those customers," he said, adding, "And I do think there are ways that we can work together, either directly or through our JV with satellite providers, to provide a complementary service and a differentiated value proposition."
Schulman reiterated that the company has no plans to offer satellite providers access to its network through mobile virtual network operator (MVNO) agreements.
"I will say, and I'll repeat it again, that there are no backdoors to any of our MVNO agreements and I see absolutely no benefit whatsoever to extending an MVNO deal to any satellite provider," he added.
An MVNO, or mobile virtual network operator, sells wireless services using another carrier's network rather than relying entirely on its own infrastructure.
Read Also: Dow Surges Over 200 Points; Verizon Shares Fall Following Q3 Results
During the call, Schulman said Verizon takes SpaceX's ambitions seriously and assumes the company will execute its plans successfully.
He argued that competing directly with established wireless carriers would require SpaceX to build a substantial terrestrial network, including 65,000 to 80,000 macro sites, backhaul infrastructure, radio access equipment and significant spectrum resources.
Schulman estimated that such a buildout could take at least four to six years and cost $300 billion to $500 billion over seven to eight years.
He also dismissed the idea that Verizon must offer Starlink network access to prevent rivals from gaining an advantage.
"There is no benefit to Verizon Communications extending an MVNO deal," Schulman said, adding that the company intends to compete aggressively if SpaceX enters the market. "We will punch back hard when that happens," he said.
Verizon shares closed down 3.49% at $43.10 on Monday, despite the company reporting its strongest third-quarter wireless subscriber growth in five years, beating earnings expectations and raising its full-year outlook.
The stock gained 0.29% to $43.23 in after-hours trading, according to Benzinga Pro.
Verizon reported adjusted third-quarter earnings of $1.31 per share, topping analysts' expectations of $1.27 .
Revenue totaled $34.31 billion, missing the $34.74 billion consensus estimate as fewer customers upgraded their devices after handset subsidies were cut.

articles.title_zh: Boeing Stock Plunges After Earnings. 737 Progress Isn’t Fast Enough.
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Third quarter earnings season is in full swing this week, with corporate results on deck from Big Tech heavy-hitters Microsoft ( MSFT ), Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ), and Amazon ( AMZN ).
Aside from Big Tech, industries from oil to chips to pharmaceuticals will be represented, as Exxon Mobil ( XOM ), Intel ( INTC ), Boeing ( BA ), Ford ( F ), and Eli Lilly ( LLY ) also open their books.
It's shaping up to be another strong earnings season. According to FactSet data , nearly a quarter of S&P 500 companies have already reported Q3 earnings so far, with an overall earnings growth rate of 29.5%. If that rate holds, it will mark the third straight quarter of earnings growth above 25%.
United Parcel Service ( UPS ) stock rose 2% on Tuesday after the courier posted third quarter results and raised its full-year guidance, signaling solid demand during the upcoming holiday season.
Revenue is expected to come in at $92.6 billion this year, up from a prior forecast of $91.2 billion. UPS also increased its adjusted earnings guidance.
Despite inflation pressures and high diesel costs, UPS is optimistic heading into the last few months of the year.
"US consumers remain resilient and the outlook for holiday demand is strong," CEO Carol Tomé said on the company's earnings call.
The company is in the middle of a multiyear turnaround plan aimed at cost-cutting and reconfiguring its delivery network.
JetBlue Airways ( JBLU ) shares rose more than 14% in premarket trading on Tuesday following the release of third-quarter results and guidance for 2027. The airline reported a loss per share of $0.60, compared to analyst estimates of $0.54. Revenue reached $2.81 billion, slightly below the $2.83 billion consensus estimate.
The airline posted an operating margin of negative 5.1% for the quarter. Operating revenue totaled $2.81 billion while operating expenses came in at $2.96 billion. The company's operating revenue increased 21% year-over-year.
Chief Executive Officer Joanna Geraghty said resilient demand and strong yields drove revenue ahead of initial expectations, allowing the company to offset more of the fuel cost increases than anticipated. She noted that Fort Lauderdale continues to deliver strong results even as the company grows capacity in that market.
Yahoo Finance's Brooke DiPalma reports:
Coca-Cola ( KO ) posted better-than-expected third quarter results and raised its earnings outlook, but the company saw slowing demand in its North American business.
Coca-Cola stock traded lower in early trading.
The company posted adjusted earnings of $0.91 per share, above the $0.88 expected by Wall Street analysts, alongside revenue of $13.4 billion, also higher than estimates of $12.9 billion.
Overall unit case volume grew by 5%, more than the roughly 3% expected. The increase was once again led by Coke Zero, which grew roughly 16% year over year. Diet Coke and Coca-Cola Light grew by 6%.
Boeing ( BA ) shrank its quarterly losses and generated cash flow in the third quarter, but its top- and bottom-line results missed Wall Street's expectations.
Revenue of $24.1 billion and an adjusted loss per share of $0.34 came in below estimates of revenue of $24.3 billion and a loss of $0.20 per share.
The company's commercial airplane unit faced higher costs in its supply chain and for production as well as a $700 million charge on its 777X program. As a result, its operating margin in that segment fell to -6.5%.
"Backlog reached a record $745B. The 737-7 and 737-10 FAA certifications and F/A-XX award are meaningful milestones, though BCA margin deterioration to -6.5% from Q2's -2.7% introduces uncertainty around the recovery pace," CFRA analysts wrote in a note following the results.
SoFi ( SOFI ) stock surged 10% in premarket trading on Tuesday after the online financial services provider lifted its 2026 outlook and reported strong results for the third quarter.
Here's what SoFi reported for Q3, compared to Wall Street analyst estimates compiled by S&P Market Intelligence:
Revenue: up 45.9% year over year to $1.39 billion, above estimates of $1.26 billion.
Adjusted earnings: $0.18, above estimates of $0.17.
Updated 2026 guidance: SoFi now expects net revenue of $5.04 billion in 2026, reflecting a 40% year-over-year increase. Adjusted EBITDA is now expected at $1.66 billion of adjusted EBITDA, and earnings per share are forecast at $0.61. Wall Street analysts were expecting 2026 earnings per share of $0.59.
The company also introduced 2027 guidance, guiding for $0.90 of earnings per share, which is above the Street's estimate of $ 0.82.
"We had exceptional Q3 results against the backdrop of any environment, but they are even more remarkable given how 2026 has unfolded," CEO Anthony Noto said. "Our focus is simple. We are adding more members, who are using more products, and generating more revenue per product to create the most value for our shareholders over the long run. In less than a decade, we have transformed SoFi from a single-product company into an everything financial app with eight different businesses each generating over $100 million in annualized revenue."
Whirlpool posted another mixed quarter as inflation and lower demand in North America took a toll.
"What is new and different is the increasingly inflationary environment that has happened from Q2 into Q3, as well as the impact of volume deleveraging which is driven by the softer demand that we have in the North America industry," Whirlpool CFO Roxanne Warner told Yahoo Finance, adding that the team is focusing on what it can control.
In the third quarter, the company reported revenue declined by nearly 9% to $3.68 billion, which was below estimates of $3.91 billion. The company reported an adjusted loss per share of $0.21, lower than the adjusted earnings per share estimate of $0.76,  per Bloomberg consensus data
Warner said that the industry hasn't caught up to the "full impact of the inflationary pressures from 2022," with inflation up 12% since then.
For that reason,  the company plans to raise prices for the third time this year, now by 7% in the fourth quarter. That follows its largest price increase in history in April, at 10%, and a 4% increase in its list prices in July.
Revenue for major appliances in its North America business fell 8.3% year over year to $2.5 billion, below Wall Street's expectations.
Whirlpool's small domestic appliance business fell almost 1% to $286 million, below the expected $314 million. However, the company said that in the third quarter, some items sold out, leading to roughly 40% year-over-year growth in US orders in October.

articles.title_orig: Pope says ‘there is no such thing as a holy war’ in message to religious leaders
articles.title_zh: Pope says ‘there is no such thing as a holy war’ in message to religious leaders
articles.content_orig:
Never before had a Pope convened representatives of the worldâs major religions for a day dedicated to peace. On 27 October 1986, John Paul II chose Assisiâthe city of Saint Francisâfor an unprecedented initiative, one destined to leave a profound mark on the history of interreligious dialogue. Forty years later, that event remains one of the most significant gestures of his pontificate and a touchstone for his successors.
There was the sight of young Jewish people offering olive branches to religious representativesâmost notably to Muslimsâa gesture that moved Cardinal Roger Etchegaray, whom Pope John Paul II had tasked with âorchestratingâ the gathering, to tears. There was the exchange of the sign of peace among the leaders of Christian Churches inside the Cathedral of San Rufino, with visible emotion etched on the faces of some of the participants. There were the leaders, shivering from the cold and huddled close together on the stage in front of the basilica, and the rainbow that appeared after a grey morningâdetails that remained in the recollections of Cardinal Etchegaray, who saw the rainbow as a sign of fraternity. These are some of the enduring images from that historic day, which was conceived to bear witness to a shared commitment to peaceâa commitment that respected diverse religious convictions, with each person engaged in prayer according to their own tradition.
Beyond mere memories, that day gave rise to what is known as the âSpirit of Assisiââa commitment by various religions to meet, engage in dialogue, and build peace together. It became a touchstone for the Churchâs magisteriumâa gesture to be interpreted, refined, and developed. Cardinal Roger Etchegaray summarized its guiding principle using a phrase from John Paul II: âTo be together to pray, but not to pray together.â Following the path set by Nostra aetate âthe Second Vatican Councilâs declaration on the Catholic Churchâs relations with non-Christian religionsâthis dialogue took on a visible form, without erasing existing differences. From Pope John Paul to his successors, the reflection has repeatedly returned to the relationship between prayer and peace, religious identity and encounter, and faith and responsibility toward humanity.
âThe very identity of the Catholic Church and its self-awareness were strengthened at Assisi,â John Paul II stated on 22 December 1986, while addressing the Roman Curia during his traditional Christmas greetingâoffering, in the process, a theological interpretation of the gathering. The Pontiff seemed to suggest that it is not enough simply to be pleased with the eventâs success; one must understand it in the light of faith. Its foundation lies in the unity of the human family, rooted in creation and the saving work of Christ. Assisi made this unity visible without obscuring religious divisions. The relationship with the Second Vatican Council is, therefore, reciprocal: the Council provides a framework for interpreting the event, while the event, in turn, helps to re-examine the Second Vatican Council with greater depth. Dialogue does not weaken ecclesial identity; rather, it can make the Church more conscious of its own mission of reconciliation.
Four years later, in the encyclical Redemptoris missio , dated 7 December 1990, John Paul II revisited this convictionâwhich he had previously expressed before the Roman Curiaâby explicitly referencing Assisi. âEvery authentic prayer is prompted by the Holy Spirit, who is mysteriously present in the heart of every person,â Pope John Paul affirmed. This was a decisive turning point: the experience helped to reshape the understanding of the role of interreligious dialogue within the Churchâs mission. Recognizing the action of the Spirit in others does not stand in opposition to the proclamation of Christ; rather, it is situated within the singular divine plan for salvation. Assisiâwith âany ambiguous interpretationâ ruled outâbears witness that respecting a person in their religious quest is, in fact, respecting the work of God within them. Dialogue, therefore, is grounded in a theological rationale, not merely a diplomatic or humanitarian one.
On 24 January 2002, John Paul returned to Assisiâthis time by trainâat a time when terrorism, hatred, and conflict loomed over the international landscape. The gathering took place just a few short months after the attacks of 11 September 2001, and the act of prayer became a public assumption of responsibility: religious communities must repudiate violenceâespecially violence that seeks to legitimize itself in the name of God. âWhoever uses religion to foment violence contradicts its most authentic and profound inspiration,â the Polish Pontiff declared. He went on to link peace with justice and forgiveness, while reaffirming the distinct nature of various forms of prayer. It was not a matter of a single, common religion, but rather a shared commitment: each person, remaining faithful to their own tradition, is called to defuse hostility. To pray does not mean to escape from history, but to engage with it responsibly. Even those who seek without believing
On 27 October 2011âthe 25th anniversary of the first prayer meeting for peaceâBenedict XVI extended an invitation to those who do not profess a faith but are nonetheless in search of the true and the good. This was not merely the addition of new guests; their presence also posed a challenge to believers. âThey are pilgrims of truth, pilgrims of peace,â Pope Benedict explained. The image of God can be obscured by the way in which religions are lived out; no one can claim God as their own exclusive possession, nor feel authorized to impose themselves upon others on that basis. In this way, Benedict XVI developed an imperative inherent to the âspirit of Assisiâ: the need to purify the way faith is practiced. In this context, Assisi calls upon believers to conduct an examination of conscience: it is not enough to condemn those who use religion to justify violence; one must also ask whether oneâs own way of living and presenting the faith truly reveals the face of a God of peace, or whether it distorts it.
âInstead, we prayed alongside one another, for one another.â In Assisi, on 20 September 2016, Pope Francis summarized with these words a continuity that explicitly excludes both syncretism and relativism. Yet, he also emphasized its fraternal dimension: it is not merely a matter of respecting the prayers of others, but of taking responsibility for one another. Dialogue must give a voice to the victims of war, to refugees, and to the poor. Prayer must be matched by concrete cooperation, and encounters must be accompanied by a commitment to address the root causes of conflicts. The threat to be overcome is not only fanaticism, but also indifference. Religious fidelity is also measured by oneâs capacity to listen to those who suffer.
â[B]elievers can draw upon the most authentic sources of their particular spiritual traditions, where there is no room for âsanctified hatredâ,â Pope Leo XIV states in paragraph 223 of the encyclical Magnifica humanitas , dated May 15, 2026. He explicitly invokes the âspirit of Assisiââfostered by John Paul II and continued by Francis, including through his dialogue with the Grand Imam of al-Azhar. The legacy of 1986 thus finds its place in social reflection on contemporary challenges: religions can counter the mentality of violence not by diluting their own convictions, but by returning to their original sources.
This is the thread that runs through forty years: the encounter is not a suspension of faith, but a test of it. For believers, Assisi continues to raise the question of whether their relationship with God can become a commitment to peace?

articles.title_orig: Cheerios introduces a Ziploc-sealed cereal bag. Finally.
articles.title_zh: Cheerios introduces a Ziploc-sealed cereal bag. Finally.
articles.content_orig:
A collaboration between Cheerios and Ziploc is bringing a practical update to grocery store shelves, offering customers an alternative to traditional bags without eliminating the familiar packaging.
Cheerios is giving its familiar cereal box an upgrade that could put an end to rolled-up bags, cereal clips and stale O's.
The General Mills brand has teamed up with Ziploc to introduce Cheerios with Ziploc PantrySeal, a resealable bag inside a traditional cereal box.
The new packaging is designed to open only partially across the top, creating a pour spout that can then be resealed to help keep cereal fresh.
YOUR FAVORITE GROCERY AND SNACK ITEMS MAY HAVE DISAPPEARED FROM STORE SHELVES IN 2026
The change comes after years of consumers asking for an easier way to close cereal bags, according to General Mills.
The company said Cheerios and Ziploc receive hundreds of thousands of requests, comments and reactions annually about cereal packaging.
Cheerios and Honey Nut Cheerios now come in new Ziploc PantrySeal packaging. (General Mills)
A December 2025 survey conducted by consumer insights platform Suzy revealed that 90% of cereal eaters take additional steps to preserve freshness after opening a box, including using clips, clothespins and cereal containers.
"Cheerios with Ziploc PantrySeal takes a small, everyday cereal frustration and finally gives consumers the simple solution they've been asking for," Emilie Knox, vice president and business unit director for Cheerios at General Mills, said in a statement.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER
It's a frustration cereal fans have also aired on social media.
"Why don't cereal companies use Ziploc type bags?" one Reddit user asked in a 2024 post that received hundreds of upvotes.
Many breakfast lovers use cereal containers to help keep Cheerios fresh. (iStock)
Other users have questioned why resealable packaging has not become standard for cereal.
"They could of did this 30 years ago. People have been asking for ages," one Reddit user wrote earlier this year.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS
"Cheerios just solved one of the biggest childhood problems," another person wrote on X after learning the news.
Some cereal eaters on social media questioned why General Mills hadn't thought of Ziploc packaging sooner. (iStock)
The new PantrySeal differs from a traditional Ziploc bag. Its zipper-style closure stops partway across the top of the bag, leaving an opening designed to make pouring easier and reduce spills.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ
The packaging will initially be offered as an option for original Cheerios and Honey Nut Cheerios rather than replacing the traditional bags in all boxes.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Cheerios with Ziploc PantrySeal became available exclusively through Walmart beginning Oct. 27 and is expected to roll out to retailers nationwide in the coming months.
